'''Takeinadane-no-Mikoto''' (''takeinadane no mikoto'') was a {{ill|gōzoku|ja|豪族}} of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} and one of the '''{{ill|Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|尾張国造}}'''. In the ''{{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}'' he is also called '''Take-Inada-no-Sukune''' ({{lang|ja|建伊那陀宿禰}}, ''take-inada no sukune'').

== Overview ==
His father was the Owari no Kuni no Miyatsuko {{ill|Otoyo-no-Mikoto|ja|乎止与命}}; his mother was {{ill|Mashikitobi-no-Mikoto|ja|眞敷刀婢命}} (daughter of {{ill|Owari-no-Ōinki|ja|尾張大印岐}}). {{ill|Miyazu-hime|ja|宮簀媛}} was his younger {{ill|sister|ja|妹}}. With his consort {{ill|Tama-hime|ja|玉姫}} (daughter of {{ill|Ōarata-no-Mikoto|ja|大荒田命}}, ancestor of the Niwa clan), he had two sons and four daughters. His son {{ill|Shiritsunane-no-Mikoto|ja|尻綱根命}} was a minister of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}. His next daughter {{ill|Shiritsuki-Tome|ja|志理都紀斗売}} was a consort of Prince {{ill|Ihokiiribiko-no-Miko|ja|五百城入彦皇子}} (a son of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ja|景行天皇}}) and mother of {{ill|Honda-no-Mawaka-no-Ōkimi|ja|品陀真若王}}. His next daughter {{ill|Kanata-Yano-Hime-no-Mikoto|ja|金田屋野姫命}} was a consort of Honda-no-Mawaka-no-Ōkimi and mother of Emperor Ōjin's empress {{ill|Naka-tsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} and two other consorts.

He served the {{ill|imperial court|ja|朝廷 (日本)|lt=imperial court}} during the reigns of Emperor Keikō and {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇}}, and is said to have accompanied {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}} as deputy general on the eastern expedition, earning military merit. He is enshrined at {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|ja|熱田神宮}}, {{ill|Utsutsu Shrine|ja|内々神社}}, {{ill|Hazu Shrine|ja|幡頭神社}}, {{ill|Hazu-Misaki Shrine|ja|羽豆神社}}, {{ill|Narumi Shrine|ja|成海神社}}, {{ill|Owaribe Shrine|ja|尾張戸神社}}, {{ill|Yakumo Shrine (Yakumo)|ja|八雲神社 (八雲町)|lt=Yakumo Shrine}}, and other shrines.

== Genealogy ==
*Father: {{ill|Otoyo-no-Mikoto|ja|乎止与命}} (descendant of {{ill|Ame-no-Hoakari-no-Mikoto|ja|天火明命}})
*Mother: {{ill|Mashikitobi-no-Mikoto|ja|眞敷刀婢命}} (daughter of {{ill|Ōinki|ja|大印岐}})
*Sister: {{ill|Miyazu-hime|ja|宮簀媛}} (consort of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊}})
*Consort: {{ill|Tama-hime|ja|玉姫}} (daughter of {{ill|Ōarata-no-Mikoto|ja|大荒田命}})
**{{ill|Otsunane-no-Mikoto|ja|尾綱根命}}
**{{ill|Shiritsuki-Tome|ja|志理都紀斗売}} (consort of {{ill|Ihokiiribiko-no-Miko|ja|五百城入彦皇子}})
***{{ill|Honda-no-Mawaka-no-Ōkimi|ja|品陀真若王}}
**{{ill|Kanata-Yano-Hime-no-Mikoto|ja|金田屋野姫命}} (consort of Honda-no-Mawaka-no-Ōkimi)
***{{ill|Takagi-Iribime-no-Mikoto|ja|高城入姫命}} (consort of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}})
***{{ill|Naka-tsu-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|仲姫命}} (empress of Emperor Ōjin; mother of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}})
***{{ill|Oto-hime-no-Mikoto|ja|弟姫命}} (consort of Emperor Ōjin)

== See also ==
*{{ill|Utsutsu Shrine|ja|内々神社}} — On the return from the eastern expedition, while Takeinadane-no-Mikoto was leading the naval force, he saw an unusual seabird and tried to catch it as a gift for Yamato Takeru, but fell into the sea of {{ill|Suruga|ja|駿河国|lt=Suruga}} and drowned. When Yamato Takeru entered the {{ill|Utsutsu Pass|ja|内津峠}} in Owari on his return, he heard the report of Takeinadane-no-Mikoto's drowning from his retainer {{ill|Kume-no-Yabara|ja|久米八腹}}, who had ridden swiftly to bring the news, and lamented "Utsutsu kana, utsutsu kana" ("Is it really true?"); enshrining the spirit is said to be the shrine's origin.
*{{ill|Hazu Shrine|ja|幡頭神社}} — Located on a cape called Miyazaki in {{ill|Nishio, Aichi|ja|西尾市|lt=Nishio City}} (Kira-chō), Mikawa Bay (Atsumi Bay). On the return from the eastern expedition, Takeinadane-no-Mikoto, who had served as banner-bearer ("hazu"), drowned in an accident in the sea off Suruga (Izu); his body washed ashore on Miyazaki Beach of this cape and was buried there by the villagers.
*Machiai-no-Ura ({{ill|Hazu-Misaki|ja|羽豆岬}}) — Near {{ill|Hazu Shrine|ja|羽豆神社}}, which enshrines Takeinadane-no-Mikoto, at Morosaki in Minamichita-chō. Morosaki is said to be where Takeinadane-no-Mikoto and his wife Tama-hime lived, and Takeinadane-no-Mikoto is said to have walked daily along the scenic Hazu-Misaki. When he set off with Yamato Takeru leading the naval force on the eastern expedition, his wife Tama-hime is said to have waited for her husband's return, and so the bay came to be called "Machiai-no-Ura" (the Bay of Waiting).
